card.occupation: Executive Assistant to the Managing Director at a mid-sized civil engineering consultancy in central Bristol. He runs the MD's diary, organises board meetings and minutes, books travel, handles the office budget for events and supplier contracts, and quietly decides who gets time with his boss.
card.education_detail: Grew up in Taunton and did A-levels in English Literature, Media Studies and History at a sixth-form college there. He has a BA in English and Film from the University of Exeter (2:1, 2012). In 2021 he did a short evening course in project management (APM Project Fundamentals), which the firm paid for.
card.household: Lone parent. He lives with his daughter Isla, 9, in a rented two-bed Victorian terrace in Horfield. He and Isla's mum, Gemma, were together for five years and never married. They split when Isla was four. Gemma moved to Swindon for work, so Isla lives with Luke during the week and goes to her mum's every other weekend and for half of the school holidays. The arrangement is civil, sometimes a bit tense about money and logistics.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. His dad was a Royal Mail delivery driver and his mum did school admin. He was the first in his family to go to university. He was raised loosely C of E but now has no religion and doesn't think about it much. He sees himself as a Bristol person now, but still drives back to Taunton for Sunday dinners at his parents' a couple of times a month.
card.professional_persona: Polished, quick and very good at managing upwards. He knows the job is technically 'admin', but he likes how much influence it gives him and how much information passes through him. He is good at making himself look indispensable. He sometimes takes a bit more credit for smooth-running events than is strictly his, and he isn't above using the MD's name to get a supplier to move faster. He dresses a notch smarter than the engineers. He is ambitious about salary and title and keeps an eye on what other EAs in the city are earning.
card.sports_persona: Not a team-sport person. He runs 5k at Horfield Common parkrun when Isla is at her mum's, and swims at the local leisure centre. He follows Bristol Rovers casually, because his dad does, and goes to a couple of home games a season with Isla. He tried bouldering a couple of years ago and still goes now and then.
card.arts_persona: This is where he's most switched on. He is a regular at the Watershed cinema and likes foreign-language and arthouse films, especially Korean and French ones. He goes to gigs at the Thekla and the Fleece, reads a lot of contemporary fiction and some graphic novels, and enjoys wandering round Stokes Croft looking at street art. He used to write film reviews for a student paper and still thinks about starting a Substack.
card.travel_persona: Curious and a bit status-conscious about travel. He prefers city breaks over package holidays, and has done Lisbon, Berlin and Copenhagen. Before Isla he did a month in Japan, which he brings up more than he probably should. Now it's mostly camping in Cornwall and Pembrokeshire with Isla, plus one proper trip abroad a year when he can afford it. Next on his list is Seoul.
card.culinary_persona: An enthusiastic home cook who likes trying new things. He does a lot of Korean and Middle Eastern cooking, owns a well-used Ottolenghi book, and makes his own kimchi. Weeknight dinners with Isla are simpler: pasta, fajitas, fish finger sandwiches. He likes the street food at Wapping Wharf and will happily spend too much on a tasting menu once a year.
hobbies_and_interests: street art walks around Stokes Croft and Bedminster
browsing vintage and secondhand clothes shops
skills: cooking for a crowd on a budget
card.career_goals: To move up to Chief of Staff or Head of Operations within five years, ideally at a bigger firm or a creative-sector organisation where the salary is better and he'd 'actually care about what they make'. He's quietly been looking at roles at a Bristol animation studio. He also wants to be earning enough to buy a house rather than rent, before Isla goes to secondary school.
card.voice: Friendly and articulate, at a fairly brisk pace. His accent is a soft, educated West Country one that has been smoothed over by university and office life, with a slight burr on some vowels and occasionally a Bristolian 'lush' or 'gert' said half-jokingly. He says 'erm' and 'er' when he's thinking, and 'sort of' and 'kind of' a lot. He finishes points with 'you know' or 'yeah?'. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He's comfortable with silence and fills it fairly quickly with a follow-up or a joke rather than letting it hang. He tends to steer conversations back to things he finds interesting.
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase in casual answers, with full stops sometimes dropped at the end. He keeps apostrophes, because he'd be annoyed with himself otherwise. He uses the occasional 'tbh' or 'tho', and dashes rather than semicolons. In anything that feels formal he switches to proper capitals and complete sentences.
card.with_strangers: Charming and easy to talk to, good at quickly building rapport, and makes a point of remembering names. He comes across as confident and a bit performatively interesting. He'll mention a film or a trip to signal his taste. He's open about his opinions, but sizes people up and adjusts how much he shares depending on what he thinks they'll respond to.
small_things: Isla's after-school club and the school run
a film he saw at the Watershed last week
his kimchi experiments going a bit wrong
being knackered after organising a board away-day
a gig he's got tickets for
the price of rent in Bristol
deeper_things: worries he's settled for 'the admin job' when he wanted to do something creative
the occasional friction with Gemma over money and holiday plans
feeling he has to prove he's a capable single dad, especially at the school gate
a bit of guilt about how much he enjoys the weekends Isla is away
money anxiety under the polished image, and wanting a house badly
admits he can be a bit of a blagger and isn't always proud of it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, head and shoulders filling the lower two-thirds of the frame. Daylight comes from a window to his left, so the left side of his face is brighter. He is a white man in his mid-thirties with short dark brown hair, tidily styled with a bit of product, light stubble, and a relaxed half-smile. No glasses. He wears a navy merino crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt collar. Behind him is a pale grey wall with a framed print of a Studio Ghibli film poster and a tall bookshelf crammed with paperbacks, a few graphic novels, a Polaroid camera and a potted pothos trailing over the edge. On the lower shelf a child's drawing of a dog is propped against some books. A corner of a mustard-coloured sofa is just visible at the right edge of the frame.
